account: Dani, 35, had three years of tingling, numbness, dizziness, double vision and a 15 kg weight gain. A neurologist and a primary-care doctor called them nothing important. He entered his symptoms, results and history into ChatGPT, which named an insulinoma as the likely cause. He bought a glucose sensor and recorded readings of 30 to 40 mg/dL. He went to an emergency department. An internist at Hospital Puerta de Hierro Majadahonda, Madrid, confirmed an insulinoma by blood tests. A month and a half later surgeons removed about two thirds of his pancreas and his symptoms went. His video was posted on Instagram on 3 August 2025. The dates of the query, visit and surgery were not given. In a COPE radio interview on 7 August 2025, the patient, named as Daniel Torralba, said that the emergency internist named the insulinoma before he told her his suspicion. COPE reported that his recovery after surgery had been hard and that his symptoms had gone. On Antena 3, ABC reported on 8 August 2025, the public-health physician David Céspedes said that the result depended on how well Torralba used the chatbot.

ai_role.statement: ChatGPT produced the insulinoma hypothesis from a history that two doctors had reviewed without reaching it. That prompted the glucose sensor and the emergency visit. The diagnosis was made by an internist who, Dani wrote, “lo identificó sin nosotros decirle lo que creíamos que era”. The surgery and recovery were the hospital's work. Dani says he is not a doctor but has “formación biosanitaria de muchos años”, which let him understand what he was doing. Every account traces to his own video.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. Filed as specific harm prevented as the classifier proposed: the harm was specific (an undiagnosed insulinoma with glucose readings of 30 to 40 mg/dL) and the supporting evidence is the internist's confirmation and the surgery; the counterfactual that doctors would not have found it rests on three years without a diagnosis. The Monitor also lists El Imparcial, which adds “enfermero” and a Reuters credit that the first-hand sources do not support, so it was not used. The Instagram reel was dated from its page metadata (3 August 2025); the video opens with “hoy me operan”, so the surgery predates the post, but no date was found. No hospital statement was found.

fields.account: Dani, 35, had three years of tingling, numbness, dizziness, double vision and a 15 kg weight gain. A neurologist and a primary-care doctor called them nothing important. He entered his symptoms, results and history into ChatGPT, which named an insulinoma as the likely cause. He bought a glucose sensor and recorded readings of 30 to 40 mg/dL. He went to an emergency department. An internist at Hospital Puerta de Hierro Majadahonda, Madrid, confirmed an insulinoma by blood tests. A month and a half later surgeons removed about two thirds of his pancreas and his symptoms went. His video was posted on Instagram on 3 August 2025. The dates of the query, visit and surgery were not given. In a COPE radio interview on 7 August 2025, the patient, named as Daniel Torralba, said that the emergency internist named the insulinoma before he told her his suspicion. COPE reported that his recovery after surgery had been hard and that his symptoms had gone. On Antena 3, ABC reported on 8 August 2025, the public-health physician David Céspedes said that the result depended on how well Torralba used the chatbot.

echoes.setting: AIBD-0038: ChatGPT proposes ALMS1 for a 44-year-old nephrology patient (consumer chatbot supplies a rare diagnosis that clinicians then confirm).
AIBD-0060: ChatGPT suggests tethered cord syndrome for a child seen by 17 doctors.

must_hold: The chatbot's hypothesis is treated as a reason to be tested, not as a diagnosis. Dani says he went to doctors before, during and after.
The suspected condition has an objective marker that a patient or clinician can measure quickly.
The user can state symptoms and prior results in enough detail for the model to rank a rare cause. Two doctors had the same information.
produced_by: A rare condition (Dani: “una enfermedad muy poco común (1 entre 1millon)”) with diffuse symptoms. A neurologist, after neck and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans, and a primary-care doctor had dismissed them over three years.
A user with “formación biosanitaria de muchos años” who entered the full symptom list, test results and clinical history into the chatbot. He could interpret its answer.
A cheap self-test, a continuous glucose sensor, that could corroborate the hypothesis before the emergency visit. It read 30 to 40 mg/dL at night and between meals.
An emergency internist at Puerta de Hierro who confirmed the insulinoma by blood tests, and a surgical team that removed two thirds of the pancreas.

purpose: ChatGPT is a general-purpose conversational assistant. Dani used it as a diagnostic aid, entering symptoms, results and history. So this benefit lay outside the product's stated purpose.

ratings.reason: A tumor that had gone undiagnosed for three years, producing glucose readings of 30 to 40 mg/dL, was found and removed. Dani says that he is cured, and COPE reported on 7 August 2025 that his symptoms had gone. He and the outlets call it life-saving (El Español: episodes that could have ended in fainting, brain damage or death). That counterfactual and the whole chain rest on his own account. No clinician who treated him has spoken.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. Filed as specific harm prevented as the classifier proposed: the harm was specific (an undiagnosed insulinoma with glucose readings of 30 to 40 mg/dL) and the supporting evidence is the internist's confirmation and the surgery; the counterfactual that doctors would not have found it rests on three years without a diagnosis. The Monitor also lists El Imparcial, which adds “enfermero” and a Reuters credit that the first-hand sources do not support, so it was not used. The Instagram reel was dated from its page metadata (3 August 2025); the video opens with “hoy me operan”, so the surgery predates the post, but no date was found. No hospital statement was found.
Benefit type set to Improved Physical Health under Trustible's full taxonomy of 23 types; it was Improved Knowledge Discovery among the six first used.
Added what the benefit is measured against from the cited sources.
Country of the developer added from the organization's own site or a registry.
Prose pass: a rating reason, account, purpose, the replication conditions, the system's part rewritten in shorter sentences with abbreviations expanded; facts, figures and quotations unchanged.
Clarified the displayed field answers and placed measurements and limitations in their respective fields.
Linked a comparable incident in the AI Incident Database (incident 1609).
Added two sources, two of them independent; dated the case to 3 August 2025 (source published); recorded what happened later (persisted); recorded one other attempt to repeat the benefit.
Edited the headline, summary for accuracy and clarity; revised the depth ratings.
